title: A surjective localized section map gives a closed immersion on a basic open
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be an affine morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], meaning that inverse images of affine opens are affine. Let $U\subseteq S$ be affine, $A=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_S)$, $B=\Gamma(f^{-1}U,\mathcal O_X)$, and $\varphi:A\to B$ its section map. For $a\in A$, suppose that the localization at $\{1,a,a^2,\ldots\}$ of the $A$-linear map $\varphi$ is surjective. Then the restriction of $f$ over the principal open $D_U(a)\subseteq S$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion].

proof.text: The basic opens have localized section rings. The universal property identifies localization of the A-linear section map with the ring map on the localized rings; this identification and its preservation of surjectivity are proved by the private helper in the Lean module.
The affine criterion turns surjectivity of the map on basic-open sections into a closed immersion of the restriction, using morphismRestrict_appTop and the isomorphism on restricted sections.
